transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I, um... I guess my manager at the restaurant thought it would be a good idea for me to come in. I've been a waitress there for a while, and, well, I guess I've been a little off lately? Nothing too terrible, I promise! Just... maybe a little distracted. 

What really scared everyone at work—and I feel so bad for worrying them, I really do—is that I started, um, sort of freezing up in the middle of service? Or I'd do things out of order. Like, the other day, I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. 

I know that sounds a little weird, right? I'm sure it's just stress or something, but I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. Does that make sense?
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling sad, empty, or less interested in things you normally enjoy?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining! But, I guess... I have been a little less interested in my usual stuff? 

Like, I don't really go for beach walks, or bake, or garden much anymore. I haven't even written in my journal in a while. And... I feel terrible saying this, because my husband is so supportive and sweet, but when he tries to talk with me lately, I mostly just sit there. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude to him, I promise! It just... I don't know, it feels like I can’t get myself to care, or even start doing anything. 

I hope I'm explaining that right. Do you think that's just normal burnout from being on my feet at the restaurant all day?
When you freeze up at work or repeat those table numbers, are you aware of what's happening around you, or does it feel like you lose time or blank out?

Um, no, I don't think I lose time or anything scary like that! I'm pretty sure I'm awake and aware the whole time. It's just... I guess my mind just gets kind of stuck? 

I know it probably looked really strange to my coworkers, and I feel so embarrassed that I worried them. But I'm definitely not blanking out or fainting or anything. I'm just standing there, and it's like I can't quite make my body do the next step, so I just... repeat the numbers to try and remind myself what I'm doing? 

I hope that doesn't sound too crazy. I mean, it's just a little harmless distraction, right? Like when you walk into a room and forget why you went in there? I'm sure it's nothing to be too worried about. Does that sound like it could just be from being tired?
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, infections, or changes in your physical health? And have you seen your primary care doctor recently to rule out things like thyroid problems or anemia?

Um, no, I don't think so! I haven't been sick or anything like that. I try really hard to take good care of myself, you know? Taking my vitamins and trying to eat right, so I've been perfectly healthy physically. 

I haven't been to my regular doctor lately, just because... well, I haven't really had a reason to go? I hope that's okay. I know I probably should go for a check-up just to be safe, especially since you mentioned the thyroid thing. I wouldn't want to be irresponsible about my health! But no, no infections or anything like that. I'm doing my best to stay healthy, I promise. Do you think I need to go see my regular doctor before we keep talking?

When did you first notice these changes—the loss of interest in activities, the difficulty engaging with your husband, and the freezing episodes at work? Did all of this start around the same time, or did some symptoms come before others?

Um, well... I guess it hasn't all happened at once. I hope I'm remembering this right, I don't want to give you the wrong timeline! 

But, um, I think this whole change in me has been building for a while now. Maybe about a year and two months? Yeah, it was right around the time the restaurant asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. Which was such a nice compliment, you know? They trusted me! But... I guess that's when I started feeling a little overwhelmed, and the freezing at work and not wanting to do my hobbies kind of crept in after that. 

I really tried to handle the new responsibilities well, I promise I did! It's just been a bit of a struggle lately. Does that timeline make sense? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it is.

When you freeze up and repeat those table numbers, do you feel disconnected from your body or your surroundings, like you're watching yourself from outside, or does it feel more like your mind just gets stuck but you're still fully present in the moment?

Um, no, I definitely don't feel like I'm watching myself from the outside or anything... strange like that. I'm right there in my body the whole time, I promise. 

It's really just like I said before, my mind just sort of... hits a little speed bump? Like I'm fully there, I know I'm standing in the dining room, I know what I'm supposed to be doing, but the gears just kind of stick for a second. So I just say the numbers to help myself get unstuck. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm losing touch with reality or anything. It's really just a silly little habit I've picked up when I get overwhelmed, you know? It's not like an out-of-body experience or anything scary. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining it right so you don't think it's worse than it actually is.

When you freeze up and repeat those table numbers, do your actions feel like they're happening automatically without you deciding to do them, or do you feel like you're consciously choosing to repeat the numbers to help yourself?

Um, I think... I mean, I'm definitely choosing to do it. It's not like my body is just acting on its own or anything scary like that! I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely out of control. 

It's more like... I consciously decide to say the numbers, just to kind of give myself a little push, you know? Like a little mental reset button that I press on purpose. It's really just a coping mechanism I came up with. I hope that's an okay way to handle it? I mean, I'm trying my best to manage the stress on my own, so I just do it to help myself stay on track. I'm not doing anything completely bizarre or automatic, I promise. That sounds right, doesn't it?

When you freeze up and repeat the table numbers at work, does this tend to happen more when you're feeling stressed or anxious in that moment, or does it happen even when you're feeling relatively calm?

Um, well... I guess it happens more when things are really busy, but... sometimes it's not even when I'm feeling super anxious. I really don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job, but I guess it did scare everyone at work a little bit. 

I just... I'd freeze up right in the middle of service. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order. Like, I remember one time I was just standing over by the soda station, holding the key to the cash drawer, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks like I was supposed to. 

I know it sounds really bad when I say it out loud, and I'm so sorry if that makes me sound like a terrible employee! I really try to be good at my job. It's just... sometimes things get a little jumbled up. Do you think that's somewhat normal when someone gets overwhelmed? I hope it doesn't mean something awful is wrong with me.

During those moments when you freeze up and repeat the table numbers, do you ever feel like things around you seem unreal or dreamlike, or like you're observing yourself from a distance—even if just slightly?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I know you asked something a little like that earlier, and I hope it's okay that my answer is still the same. It never feels like a dream or anything unreal like that. The restaurant, the noise, the customers... everything is very, very real when it happens. 

I'm just standing right there in the middle of it all. I promise I'm not floating away or watching myself from afar or anything that sounds too crazy. I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, but I definitely don't have anything like that going on. It's a good sign that I don't feel like I'm in a dream, right? I really hope that means I'm still doing okay overall.

When you're standing there repeating the table numbers, do you ever feel confused about what time it is, where you are, or how long you've been standing there—or does everything feel clear and normal in terms of time and place?

Oh, no, um... everything is totally clear as far as where I am and all of that. I know I'm at work, I know what shift it is... I'm definitely not confused about that. 

I mean, I guess maybe I might lose track of like, a minute or two, just because I'm so focused on getting the numbers out? But I always know exactly where I'm standing and what time of day it is. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm completely out of touch with reality or anything like that. I know exactly what's going on around me, I promise. 

That's a good sign, isn't it? That I still know where I am? I just want to make sure you know I'm not totally losing my mind or anything. I really hope I'm answering these right for you.

When you're standing there repeating the table numbers, do you feel emotionally numb or disconnected from your feelings—like you're going through the motions but not really feeling anything—or do you feel your emotions normally?

Um, well... I guess I do feel a little... flat? But it's not just when I'm repeating the numbers. It's kind of... a lot of the time lately. I really hope that doesn't sound too bad. 

It's just that I used to do a lot of things, you know? Like, I loved going for walks on the beach, and baking, and I had a little garden... I even used to write in my journal a lot. But lately, I just... I don't really do any of that much anymore. 

And, um, my husband tries to talk to me, and I know I should be more engaged, I really do! But I mostly just sit there. It just feels like... like I can't get myself to care, or to even start doing anything. I'm really sorry, I know that sounds like I'm being a terrible wife, and I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or giving up. It's just hard to feel much of anything right now. 

Is it somewhat normal to feel a little disconnected like that when you're overwhelmed? I really hope it's something that will just pass.

When you're going through your day and feeling that flatness you mentioned—like you can't get yourself to care or do things—do you ever feel like your emotions or thoughts don't quite belong to you, or like you're observing your own life from the outside looking in?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I know you asked something kind of similar earlier, about watching myself from the outside, and... um, I hope it's okay, but my answer is still no to that. 

Even when I'm feeling really flat and just sitting there, I'm definitely still... me. I'm in my own body, and my thoughts always belong to me. They might be a little quiet right now, or I guess just not very motivated, but they're absolutely mine. I promise I don't feel like I'm watching a movie of my life or that someone else is putting thoughts in my head or anything scary like that. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm completely detached from reality. I'm just having a hard time getting moving lately, that's all. But it's a really good thing that I still feel like my thoughts are my own, right? I really hope that means I'm not doing too badly and that I'm giving you the right answers.

Over the past year or so, have you noticed changes in how fast or slow you move or speak? For example, do you feel like you're moving in slow motion, or have people mentioned that you seem to be talking more slowly than usual?

Um, no... no, I haven't noticed anything like that at all. 

I mean, since I work as a waitress, I really have to stay on my toes and keep moving, you know? If I were moving in slow motion, I think I'd be in a lot of trouble at work! So I definitely feel like I'm moving at a normal pace. And no one has said anything about me talking too slowly, either. My husband hasn't mentioned anything like that to me, and my boss hasn't complained. 

I really try my best to keep up with everything and not let anyone down. I hope that's what you were hoping to hear? I just want to reassure you that physically, I'm getting around just fine. That means I'm doing okay in that area, right? I really hope so.

Have you ever had any head injuries, concussions, or accidents that involved hitting your head? And are you currently taking any medications—even over-the-counter ones—or have you started any new medications in the past year or so?

Oh, um... no. No head injuries or concussions or anything like that. I've never been in any kind of accident where I hit my head. I try to be really careful, so... I've been pretty lucky there. 

And for medications, no, I'm not taking anything at all right now. I haven't started anything new in the last year, and I don't really even take over-the-counter stuff. Maybe just an ibuprofen once in a great while if my feet hurt after a long shift, but definitely not lately. 

I promise I'm not leaving anything out! I know sometimes people forget to mention things they take, but I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. That's probably a good thing, right? That my head is fine and I'm not taking any pills? I really hope that helps you rule some bad things out and makes your job a little easier.

You mentioned you haven't been sick recently, but I want to make sure—in the year or so before these changes started, did you have any significant infections, high fevers, or serious illnesses that you recovered from?

Um, no, definitely not. I've actually been really healthy physically. No bad infections or... or high fevers or anything like that. 

I always try to take really good care of myself, you know? I make sure to wash my hands a lot and do all the right things, especially since I'm around so many people at the restaurant all day. I wouldn't want to get anyone sick, and I really can't afford to miss shifts anyway. So I haven't had any serious illnesses at all. 

That's... that's a good sign, right? I really hope it helps that my physical health has been so good. I'm just trying my best to give you all the right details so I'm not making your job too difficult. Am I doing okay with these answers?

In the year or so before you started feeling this way—before the restaurant promoted you to the evening shift lead role—did you have any kind of surgery, hospitalization, or major medical event, even if you felt like you recovered completely from it?

Oh, no... no surgeries or anything like that. I've never been in the hospital for any major medical events. 

I've always been pretty lucky, honestly. I just try to stay healthy so I can keep up with my shifts, especially since they gave me that promotion to shift lead. I'd really hate to let them down by having to be out in the hospital or something. I take my responsibilities really seriously. 

So, no, nothing like that at all. I hope a boring medical history is a good thing? I just really want to be helpful and make sure I'm answering everything exactly how you need me to. I'm giving you the right kind of information, aren't I?

You mentioned the freezing episodes and loss of interest started building around the time you got promoted to evening shift lead about a year and two months ago. Did these changes start right around that same time, or did they begin a few weeks or months after the promotion?

Um, yeah, it was... it was right around that same time. About a year and two months ago, when they asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. 

I guess that's when this whole change in me started building. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I couldn't handle the promotion or anything! I was really grateful they trusted me with it. But, yeah, looking back, that's when things started feeling... different. Like the freezing up and just not caring about things as much. It wasn't like a switch flipped overnight, but it definitely started building up right around then.

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining the timeline clearly enough for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact details you need.

In the few months right before you got promoted to evening shift lead—so maybe around a year and three or four months ago—did you have any kind of illness with a high fever, or a bad infection, or anything like that? Even if it seemed minor at the time or you felt like you recovered completely?

Um, no, definitely not. I really didn't have anything like that. No fevers, no infections... nothing at all before the promotion. 

Like I said, I've always been really good about my health. I don't want you to think I was dragging myself to work sick or anything before they gave me the lead position! I would never do that. I was perfectly healthy, feeling completely fine. I really pride myself on being reliable and taking good care of myself. 

So, no, nothing like that at all in those months before. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I hope it's helpful that I didn't have any kind of sickness like that. I'm trying to be as clear as possible for you. Am I giving you what you need?

Before you got promoted to the evening shift lead position—so going back further, maybe a year and a half or two years ago—did you ever go through a period where you felt unusually sad, depressed, or hopeless for weeks at a time? Or on the flip side, did you ever have a period where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like you could do anything?

Um... no, no, I've never had anything like that. I've always been pretty even-keeled, you know? 

I definitely wasn't sad or depressed. I've always tried to keep a positive attitude, especially at work. People always say I'm good at keeping morale up, which is probably why they wanted me for the lead position. And I've never had a time where I didn't need sleep or felt... out of control with energy, either. I just get my normal rest and go to work. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm unstable or that my moods are all over the place. I've always been very steady.

Is that... is that normal? I mean, it's good that I haven't had those kinds of mood swings, right? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you the right kind of background.
